messages.content: Charlotte host finally sent the badge QR. One annoying update: staff garage won’t accept visitors before 7:00 a.m. Can you sanity-check the airport-to-hotel plan and both teaching mornings?

What should I do Friday with the garage not opening until 7?
Leave Homewood around 6:45-6:50. That should put you at the garage just after 7:00 and at the badge desk/admin corridor around 7:10-7:15. Earlier than 6:40 just risks sitting outside the garage.
And Saturday plus Sunday airport?

Saturday: leave around 7:10 unless the host moves the start earlier; use staff garage Level 2, east elevator, admin corridor badge desk, then north rehab wing. Sunday return still works: leave the hotel by 10:45, return Avis before noon, and keep the 1:50 p.m. CLT-TPA flight. I’ll mark Charlotte closed with no grocery stop before hospital setup and the first-night fridge/coffee routine.

messages.content: Charlotte is wrapped. I registered for the pediatric rehab conference in Denver, April 16-18. I have a Thursday afternoon lab and a Saturday morning breakout. I want to arrive Wednesday with enough room to check in and look at the meeting room, then come home Sunday afternoon if the flights are reasonable.
Got it: Tampa to Denver, Wednesday April 15 to Sunday April 19. Do you want me to compare the official conference block against a nearby suite setup, or start with flights?
Both, but group it by practicality. I’m not chasing the absolute cheapest if it creates a tight arrival or a weird room situation.

Then the flight pattern matters first. I found three sensible buckets: most practical is a Wednesday midday nonstop TPA-DEN, about 11:35 a.m. to 1:42 p.m., paired with a Sunday 2:10 p.m. DEN-TPA return, around $418-$435 round trip. Cheapest is a late Wednesday connection through Dallas or Atlanta, arriving Denver around 10:15 p.m., about $300-$315. Early-arrival option is a 7:00-ish a.m. connection landing before noon, about $360, but it makes Wednesday longer than necessary.
The late connection sounds like false savings if I need to see the room Wednesday.

I agree. It saves roughly $100 but gives up the whole setup buffer. The midday nonstop should get you downtown around 3:00-3:20 if bags and rideshare behave. That leaves room for hotel check-in, food, and a room walk-through if the conference allows it.
What about the Sunday return choices?

Best fit is the 2:10 p.m. nonstop home; leave downtown around 10:45-11:00 and you have a calm DEN buffer. There is a cheaper 12:05 p.m. return, but it compresses the morning and makes Denver airport feel like the schedule driver. There is also a 5:20 p.m. return, but that gets you home late enough to make Monday less pleasant.
Okay. Hotel block now. I saw a few grumpy reviews but couldn’t tell if they were normal conference-hotel complaints.

Two options look worth comparing. The headquarters block is the convenience pick: attached or next door to the meeting space, $229 before tax, fitness room, but recent ratings are mixed around 3.8-3.9 and the block is run-of-house bedding. They’ll only note a fridge request, not guarantee one. The suite hotel is the predictability pick: about 8-12 minutes by rideshare, stronger ratings around 4.3-4.4, cancellable queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool. It does not have a hot tub.
So the official block wins only on location?

Mostly, yes. It also reduces weather and traffic variables on conference mornings. But the room caveats are real: run-of-house bedding, fridge only by request, and several recent complaints about noise and slow elevators. It is practical if walking access is the top concern. It is less practical if you need predictable room setup.
I do not want to land, teach the next day, and discover I have no fridge or an odd bed setup.

Then I would not book the headquarters block unless they put bedding and fridge in writing. The suite hotel is cleaner operationally: queen studio confirmed, coffee/fridge listed in-room, stronger review pattern, and enough space to reset between sessions. The trade-off is the daily short rideshare and no hot tub.
How bad is the commute to the venue?

Not bad, but it is still a variable. Plan 8-12 minutes by rideshare in normal downtown traffic, or closer to 15-18 minutes if pickup is slow. I’d budget leaving the suite hotel 30 minutes before you need to be in the conference room, especially Thursday before the lab.
Can you give me the short version: lead plan, cheap plan, and don’t-do-it plan?

Lead plan: Wednesday midday nonstop, Sunday 2:10 p.m. return, suite hotel. Costs more, but protects arrival setup and room reliability. Cheap plan: late Wednesday connection plus the suite hotel; lower airfare, but no useful Wednesday buffer. Don’t-do-it plan: late connection plus headquarters block without written bedding/fridge confirmation; that stacks arrival risk on top of room uncertainty.
What needs confirmation before booking?

Four items: conference presenter check-in or room-preview window on Wednesday; whether the headquarters hotel can guarantee bedding and fridge rather than just request them; suite hotel cancellation deadline and whether the listed queen studio is still available; and seat/fare rules on the flights, especially whether the Sunday afternoon fare includes seat selection or pushes it to check-in.
Put the lead in the file but don’t book yet. I’ll ask the conference about the Wednesday check-in window and send one more note to the headquarters hotel.

Added as the tentative Denver lead: April 15 midday nonstop TPA-DEN, Sunday April 19 afternoon return, and the nearby suite hotel with queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool. Caveats noted plainly: no hot tub, short rideshare to the venue, not in the official block, and booking should wait for the Wednesday check-in window plus one last headquarters-hotel answer on bedding and fridge.

messages.content: Denver answers came in. Presenter check-in is Wednesday 4:30 to 6:30. Headquarters hotel still won’t guarantee bedding or fridge, just says they’ll note it. Can we book the safer flight and the suite hotel if the fare hasn’t gone crazy?

Yes. The Wednesday nonstop has gone up but not wildly: United TPA-DEN 11:35 a.m.-1:42 p.m., paired with Sunday DEN-TPA 2:10 p.m.-7:39 p.m., is $438 in Main Cabin before any seat fee. The late connection is still cheaper, but it lands after 10:00 p.m., so it no longer fits the 4:30-6:30 presenter check-in.
Before booking, what are the seat and fare caveats?

Main Cabin includes carry-on and standard changes for airline credit, but no prepaid checked bag. Outbound has included window seats available. On the Sunday return, the included seat map is picked over: free windows are gone, but there is a paid preferred window at $29. Otherwise I can take an included aisle or set a reminder to try for a window at check-in.
Use the paid return window if it stays under $30. No checked bag.

Hotel check before I commit: the suite hotel has the queen studio available, coffee maker and mini-fridge listed in-room, fitness room and indoor pool confirmed, no hot tub, and it is still a short rideshare to the venue rather than the official block. Cancellable until April 13 at 6:00 p.m. Total with taxes is about $1,006 for four nights. Okay to book flights plus hotel?
Yes. The no-hot-tub and rideshare caveats are fine. I want the predictable room.

Booked the flights. United confirmation U7D4QK: Wednesday Apr 15 TPA 11:35 a.m. to DEN 1:42 p.m.; Sunday Apr 19 DEN 2:10 p.m. to TPA 7:39 p.m. Main Cabin, no prepaid checked bag. Seats: 18A window outbound included, 21A window return with the $29 preferred-seat fee.
That still gives enough Wednesday margin, right?
Yes. If the flight is close to schedule, you should be downtown around 3:00-3:20. That leaves time to check in or store bags, get oriented, and make the 4:30-6:30 presenter window without sprinting.
And the hotel reservation went through?

Reserved Denver Downtown Suite Hotel, confirmation DDS-91438, Apr 15-19. Queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, indoor pool, no hot tub. Rate is cancellable until Apr 13 at 6:00 p.m.; after that the first night is penalty.
Please put the airport and venue timing in the file so I don’t have to redo it later.

Denver plan is now booked: fly in Wednesday midday, aim to be downtown by 3:15, presenter check-in 4:30-6:30, use rideshare from the suite hotel to the venue and budget 30 minutes door to room on conference days.
